How to read this comparison
  • If the unfiltered engine already looks wrong, changing glyphs cannot fix its motion.
  • If reference motion stays readable through the shared grid but the engine does not, granularity alone is not the cause.
  • The contrast toggle changes ink and fill only. It never changes cell size or adds a separate sprite resolution.
  • Both sequences are sampled at twelve phases per cycle to avoid giving the engine an unfair smoothness advantage. Reference frame 0 is near a foot-contact pose; alignment is approximate, not motion capture registration.
  • The historical subject is seen slightly obliquely. Adjust the rig angle for visual comparison. There are differences in anatomy, clothing, illumination and camera perspective.
  • The reference GIF's four-second loop is an editorial playback choice. Here it is retimed to the engine's 1.66-second stride, not used to estimate real walking speed.

The engine figure occupies 160 pixels of the original 1280 × 854 scene, then is magnified equally in all panels. This is a diagnostic enlargement of existing cells, not extra detail for people.
